prospect.name: Tommy
prospect.family_status: Engaged, getting married late September 2026; fiancee is a nurse; no children; moved city, started a new job and bought a house in the past year
prospect.training_background: Lifelong runner (several marathons) and cyclist, cardio-heavy. Has self-coached strength training for about three years using at-home equipment, with little perceived progress. Self-rates mobility 9/10 and flexibility 5/10, cannot touch toes.
prospect.medical: History of tendinitis and knee problems; a hip injury in high school. No current pain, no active condition or treatment disclosed.

signals: 32, 5'11", 180 lb, self-rated mobility 9/10, trains and moves daily - not deconditioned
Frames the ask as good-to-great: upper body size, abs, flexibility from 5 to 9
Blocker is expertise, not motivation: 'I'm pretty motivated' / 'really what I'm looking for is expertise in terms of knowledge'
Counter-signal to optimizer: a wedding budget constraint made price a live issue, so price was not purely a quality signal

goals.text: Build upper body - chest, shoulders, arms - and get abs showing
Functional strength so he can keep moving and stay injury-free as he ages
Improve flexibility from a self-rated 5/10 to a 9 or 10, e.g. touch his toes
Be in the best shape possible for his wedding in late September
Find a routine he can hold for years, not just three months
Get back the quiet confidence and calm he feels when training consistently

pains.text: Three years of self-coaching strength with little to show: 'No, not a ton. And so that's why I'm kind of looking around.'
No strength-training knowledge base to program for himself - can self-coach running and cycling but not lifting
Has never found a routine that sticks: 'I don't know that I've really hit my stride with finding the right routine.'
A year of transitions - new job, new city, house purchase, wedding planning - caused training to lapse
Demanding job with weekend hours limits session length to roughly 30-40 minutes
Chronically tight from running; past tendinitis, knee and hip injuries sit in the back of his mind
Dislikes the gym environment, so gym-based solutions do not hold

objections.raw_quote: I think we just have a general deal that when we spend money, we are on the same page ahead of time. So I am still very interested in this. I think that we both will here very soon. I just want to talk with her about it before we spend too much money on this.
objections.rep_response: Confirmed the fiancee knew about the call and was supportive, asked what her reaction to 6k would be, floated a small refundable commitment to hold the decision, then when that was declined booked a three-way call for the next day at 2pm and sent the calendar invite live on the call.

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, I think it's something I want to get started on. I do want to just... Yeah. Sleep on it overnight in terms of cost, but the program itself, yes.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the hesitation to cost only ('is that just mainly around the cost itself?'), confirmed the programme itself was a yes, then moved to the spouse angle rather than running the think-about-it play.

evidence: Prospect verbally committed to the programme but not the spend: 'Committed to everything else. But again, just in planning a wedding, we have a budget that we're working through.'
No payment taken and no payment link mentioned anywhere on the call
Concrete next step booked and accepted live: a three-way call with the fiancee the following day at 2pm, invite sent and accepted on the call
Counter-evidence that this is closer to a yes than a maybe: 'the answer is not, no, the answer is, I just want to be honest about that'
outcome.next_step: Three-way call with the prospect and his fiancee the following day at 2pm to answer her questions and, if green-lit, start immediately.

notable.note: Rep volunteered a personal WhatsApp line and a recurring personal check-in outside the packaged offer, explicitly saying it is not a standard part of the team's service. Also, no financial-picture questions were asked and no payment plan was mentioned even though budget was the single stated blocker.

quality.notes: Extensive label swapping throughout. Prospect answers are repeatedly attributed to 'Richard Claessen (Primal Instinct)' (e.g. 00:08:54 'I want to try to avoid injury for as long as I can') and rep questions to 'Ttr' (e.g. 00:07:13 'so take me through, like, how can we potentially help you?'). Many turns contain both speakers concatenated. Roles were assigned from content only. The prospect's label 'Ttr' is a device/initials artefact; his name Tommy comes from the rep addressing him directly.
